channels.name: Identity, Auth & Access Control
channels.evidence: All five authorization checks pass, and ?all_projects=1 no longer defeats the task_key scope boundary — a client-controlled query string had been able to read any issue by key across projects, defeating the 404 whose stated purpose was preventing exactly that. Verified: scoped lookup of a foreign key returns 404 with and without the param, while a scope-blind script still resolves it. Held back from the goal because authentication is still three shared passwords doubling as their own session tokens — no users, no logout, no rate limiting.
channels.goal_text: builderz-labs — per-agent API keys and viewer/operator/admin roles over real sessions, replacing three shared passwords that double as their own tokens.

channels.name: Work Management API (MC API)
channels.evidence: The code-review lifecycle completes AND the bug lifecycle is unblocked. `environment` was required by a validator and was not a column, so a bug moving defined->open answered 400 without it and 500 with it — every bug in this installation was stuck, in both directions, and the Bug Details panel read "No bug details provided" on every bug ever opened. Now 200 with the fields stored. A body carrying the phantom column returns 422 NAMING the real columns rather than 500, which matters because lib/agent-queue.ts still instructs the Tester agent to send it — the outage was one agent run from returning. The MC API also no longer routes work to agents that do not exist. Held back: limit=0 still means every matching row and two callers use it to read one integer, and the API still returns raw CHECK constraint text for an invalid enum value.
channels.goal_text: Linear's issue list — server-side paging with an exact total, so no screen ever shows a number computed from a truncated slice.

channels.name: Portability & Host Independence
channels.evidence: The recorded evidence was wrong on two of three clauses — the SQLite adapter IS registered and Supabase is NOT a hard requirement — and the third clause, "no proven clone-to-running path", was true only because nobody had run it. It has now been run for real: a throwaway copy of .git, git clone FROM the copy so the working tree was never touched, then only what a newcomer would do. Setup exits 0 in 1.7s with no prompts, 54 tables and 18 ledger rows, doctor exits 0, server ready in 1974ms, health reports db.reachable with missingTables empty, login 200, and POST /api/issues creates an issue and reads it back — with NO CLOUD ACCOUNT at any point. Held back by one step, and it is step 1: npm install from the committed lockfile runs node-gyp on better-sqlite3 and dies on a host with no C++ toolchain, because lockfile v3 has no slot for that package gypfile:false declaration. The obvious workaround was REJECTED — ignore-scripts in .npmrc would make install succeed and silently disable the prebuild guards, trading a visible failure for an invisible one.
channels.goal_text: builderz-labs — SQLite and one start command, no Redis, Postgres or Docker. Clone it, run it, working app on any OS with no cloud account.

channels.name: LLM Provider Independence
channels.evidence: This channel carried a FALSE evidence string for several waves: "66 remaining references — chat still routes to a cloud host the owner has ruled out". A builder measured it and both halves are wrong. Live code across app/lib/components/hooks contains ZERO references to the ruled-out provider, comments stripped or not. Chat routes to LLM_BASE_URL, which is http://localhost:11434/v1 — proven live rather than read: a cloud model id returns 400 naming the local endpoint it is not present in, and a local qwen2.5-coder id returns 200 with an SSE stream. The model list is proxied from that endpoint, so it is live rather than hardcoded, and a new test locks the dangerous shape — an unreachable or empty roster must error naming the URL and must NOT fall back to a constant. The provider is genuinely a base URL: selection is an env var, resolveProvider refuses to default to a cloud host, and tiers resolve against the live roster rather than a static map. A new guard derives its banned set from the "Never X" bullets in HANDOFF.md rather than carrying its own list. Held back: two migration CHECK constraints still ADMIT a ruled-out connection type on a legacy table with no callers, and two CLI runtimes map tiers to hardcoded vendor ids because their provider is a binary, not a base URL — there is no seam to move them onto.
channels.goal_text: LiteLLM — the provider is a base URL, not a code branch. Open WebUI — the model list is read live from that endpoint, never hardcoded.

channels.name: Agent Visualization Fidelity
channels.evidence: The Office states '0 of 30 agents report a workspace folder — the positions on the floor below are decorative', computed from the field so the wording self-corrects if agents ever report one. That is the honest version of a surface that previously implied position meant something. Held back: GET /api/tasks 404s on every poll from two independent pollers, 30s and 60s, and the roster still lists Kemuni SME and Vespera SME — agents for projects that do not exist.
channels.goal_text: pixel-agents — every character state derives from real Claude Code hook events, and a speech bubble appears when an agent is waiting on you.

channels.name: Data Layer & Schema Management
channels.evidence: Migration 066 restores four columns that a live validator required and the schema did not have — environment, steps_to_reproduce, expected_behavior, actual_behavior — and DELIBERATELY does not add test_status, with both halves of that reasoning in the migration comment. The evidence for the split was measured, not argued: across 3,078 production rows in the Supabase export the stored test_status disagreed with the derived value on 372 of them, 12.1 percent, with passed sitting on rows whose tester and designer were both still pending. A stored duplicate of a derived value that was already wrong one time in eight. A new no-phantom-columns guard compares every column named in live code against the LIVE schema and is proven in both directions across writes, filters, selects and query strings — and states in its own header the case it would NOT catch, which is the interface declaration where this defect lived longest.
channels.goal_text: builderz-labs — migrations run at first DB access, so starting the app creates the schema. No migrate command to know about, no colliding prefixes.

channels.name: Observability & Honest Reporting
channels.evidence: Seven guards now — invented-projects, unscoped-issues, no-secrets, silent-empty, dead-modules, cloud-provider, phantom-columns — and every one proven in both directions. Two more landed this wave: cloud-provider derives its banned set from the "Never X" bullets in HANDOFF.md so it cannot drift from the decision record, and phantom-columns compares code against the live schema. The most valuable output was a FAKE GREEN caught in the one tool a newcomer runs first: npm run doctor printed a raw Require stack dump, then said "OK — this host can run Todero" and exited 0, while health on the same checkout reported db.reachable false. It resolved the provider NAME from env without ever touching the driver; it now opens an in-memory database and round-trips a row. Held back: each new guard names a real blind spot in its own header rather than implying coverage it does not have.
channels.goal_text: Paperclip — full tool-call tracing and an audit log per ticket. LangSmith — drill from a cost number to the run and step that caused it.

channels.name: Work Management UI
channels.evidence: The goal is Linear: a board that refuses a move the server rejected, and never renders an empty state over an error. Both halves hold now. The move sheet only offers destinations it can finish: requirements are a function of (row, destination) rather than destination alone — an epic passes refined where a task needs test_tier — so the predicate takes the row and returns a verdict. Fields it can supply are collected inline and sent in the same PATCH; what the board genuinely cannot supply is shown DISABLED WITH THE REASON rather than hidden, on the argument that an operator who cannot reach code_review is worse off than one told what it needs. No raw database text reaches the operator, proven against a REAL 500 rather than a simulated one. And sending a card back to Backlog answered 403 to the workspace owner — the most common gesture on any board — because that guard was the only actor check in the route without the owner bypass the other two have. Held back: the 10-open cap and the one-at-a-time lane are deliberately not predicted, because they depend on other rows and can change between render and tap.
channels.goal_text: Linear — a board that refuses a move the server rejected, and never renders an empty state over an error.

channels.name: Agent Fleet Operations
channels.evidence: Liveness carries PROVENANCE now, not just a value. A registration with no check-in inherited its creation time as lastSeenAt and Fleet worded it as a hook event — measured with the heartbeat store readable and empty: 'last event 4m ago' over zero events. AgentDto now carries lastSeenSource, each builder sets it from the branch it took, and the classifier returns never for any non-heartbeat source — the same refusal it already made for an unread store. CrewTab fails CLOSED when the field is missing, and /api/connect stops discarding the heartbeat write warning. Four states, all reachable, all sourced.
channels.goal_text: builderz-labs — POST /api/connect registers an agent and returns the URLs to use next; 30s heartbeats, offline at 10min. Liveness from data, never an array.

channels.name: Run Safety & Enforcement
channels.evidence: runTouchedPaidProvider read cost_usd and never provider, while the screen printed the design rule verbatim — false against a step whose own row said anthropic. It reads provider now, and the word 'paid' left BOTH the code and the screen, because run_steps records WHICH provider and never whether it charges: calling one paid would have replaced one fabrication with another. Two more lies in the same panel are gone — a dollar total divided by steps that recorded no dollars, and a cost-bearing group vanishing from the bars while its dollars stayed in the total. Held back: nothing writes run_steps in production, so the shipped surface is still empty.
channels.goal_text: Paperclip — budgets per agent, and at the limit they stop. Portkey — the cap is enforced in the request path, outside the agent, so it cannot be reasoned past.

channels.name: Learning & Memory Loop
channels.evidence: The builder found the artboard was WRONG and said so rather than building to it: the single 1,300-token budget is two budgets — identity, 1300 x 6 = 7,800, always loaded, and retrieval, 1,300, per task. Both now render separately with their real constants, and drift tests fail if either constant moves. Six artboard elements could not be sourced and each renders an explicit absence naming what is missing rather than a plausible number. A critic called it the most honest surface in the app. Held back: nothing populates the store on this instance, so every panel is an honest empty.
channels.goal_text: Hermes Agent — records what it tried and failed after each task, retrieves it on similar ones by FTS5, and caps in-context memory so overflow errors instead of truncating.

channels.name: Navigation & Deep Linking
channels.evidence: Six destinations, path-based URLs, and renamed views resolve through LEGACY_VIEW_MAP so an old bookmark lands where it meant to rather than on the destination default. A smoothing pass then found five of six Settings views unlinkable — parseURL tested LEGACY_TAB_MAP before isDestinationId, and that branch discards the view segment — which meant the Connections card holding credential custody sat at the one URL that could not be reloaded. Fixed and verified through a reload. Held back: the palette cannot open an issue because no issue route exists.
channels.goal_text: Slack — every message has a permalink that opens it in context. LangSmith — every trace has a URL. Linear — any view is a link. No screen unreachable.

channels.name: Approval & Human-in-the-loop
channels.evidence: Every refusal path now reaches the operator. ApprovalCard claimed a label could not promise an effect the server would refuse; the check it cited compares type-key sets only, and two of four live cards offered a button the server answers 409 to. approveGate runs the route own preflightDecision and shows the server reason VERBATIM for every code, disabled rather than absent. The audit trail records refusals and failed effects as failed. Held back: decided_by is still a client-side literal while mc-auth exists, and requestApproval() has no callers, so approving repairs rather than gates.
channels.goal_text: Slack — the difference between new, for-you, and a thread you are in. Grok Bot — surfaces only what needs you. You approve from your phone; Todero sends.

channels.name: Pipeline Fidelity
channels.evidence: All 16 lifecycle statuses map across 8 columns, each exactly once, as data a test enumerates — and the completeness test is red in both directions: unmapping a status fails 5 of 53 saying an issue in it would be invisible, inventing one fails 3 of 53 naming it. The lane by agent is real: 29 lanes from 28 live roster rows, with the 22 idle agents each still named, so an agent with nothing to do is distinguishable from one that does not exist. A smoothing pass then found BoardTab — the DEFAULT Work view — dropping six statuses silently: header reading "19 issues" over columns holding 12, with no warning that seven cards had gone. Not hypothetical: the MC API writes the status "underway" on two paths, so it happens in normal operation. Its three-column simplification stays, but its catch-all chip is now DERIVED from VALID_STATUSES minus everything already placed, so a status added to the lifecycle tomorrow appears rather than vanishing. Verified zero uncovered. Held back: 7 of 15 move-sheet transitions still cannot complete, two of them surfacing raw SQLite constraint text to the operator.
channels.goal_text: Linear — group a board by any dimension, every column a real status. Plane — swim lanes. Todero adds a lane per agent, so you see what each one is working through.

channels.name: Customer Conversations
channels.evidence: From nothing to a store, a lifecycle and a surface. The owner rule — 'You approve; Todero sends' — is a CHECK CONSTRAINT, not a policy in a route: state=sent with approved_at NULL throws in both dialects. The builder proved that is not decorative by rebuilding the same schema WITHOUT the checks and showing the identical inserts accepted. An agent can draft and cannot approve its own draft (201 then 403). No transport exists, proven mechanically: grep for fetch/http/axios/WebSocket across every owned file returns three hits, all same-origin. Held back: no inbound webhook and no provider — WhatsApp is the benchmark and no provider decision exists — and the card was wired at the wave boundary but has not been watched rendering in a browser.
channels.goal_text: Slack — a reply threads instead of drowning the channel. Grok Bot — drafts while you are away, surfaces only what needs approval. You approve; Todero sends.

channels.name: Commerce Operations
channels.evidence: Orders, products and inventory are objects with two real actions — inventory adjust and order fulfilment — both persisted and re-read from the database rather than from React state. Money is an integer count of minor units, and the load-bearing reason is that THE TWO HOSTS MUST AGREE: Postgres has exact NUMERIC, SQLite has none, so a NUMERIC column would be exact on Postgres and an IEEE float on the host a fresh clone gets — and every Postgres-run test would still pass. An unknown currency is refused rather than assumed to have two decimals, because assuming is a silent 100x error. Commerce fails closed harder than issues: no all-projects mode at all. Held back: no provider integration, no commerce:* permission (reads borrow projects:read), the inventory adjust is read-modify-write rather than atomic, and the card is wired but unwatched.
channels.goal_text: Shopify admin — orders, catalog and inventory as first-class objects you can act on, not a dashboard that only reports what happened.

channels.name: Multi-tenancy & Identity
channels.evidence: Still deliberately post-MVP per HANDOFF — authentication remains three shared passwords and every record is global. Two things moved: GET /api/agent-responsibilities stopped answering 200 with a full payload for any business_id (now 404 unknown_hub), and project scope resolution for conversations and commerce collapsed into one lib/scope.ts whose surface descriptor is DATA rather than strategy — it can change what a refusal is called, never whether there is one. The channel stays near zero until real sessions and per-tenant isolation exist.
channels.goal_text: Linear — sign in and see only your workspace. Anyone runs Todero for their own business and projects, isolated from everyone else.

channels.name: Secrets & Credential Custody
channels.evidence: The live bot token is out of source in both copies, and it was already DEAD — a builder posted it to Discord and got 401, so every notification had been failing silently. Migration 059 puts the credential in a separate table from the connection, so a leak requires a deliberate second query rather than any select(*). check-no-secrets.js now names its own coverage and ends 'This is not a statement that the tree contains no credential', and its credential-name rule is case-insensitive after a critic measured that SCREAMING_SNAKE-only left camelCase uncovered. Held back: a critic found credential_env_var was an arbitrary env-var READ ORACLE readable by a viewer — now scoped to the provider's declared variable — and resolveHubDiscord still has zero callers, so the operator can add Discord to a hub and nothing reads the row.
channels.goal_text: Doppler / Vercel env — secrets encrypted at rest, scoped per service, revocable without redeploy, and never printed. Todero holds delegated tokens only.

channels.name: Search & Findability
channels.evidence: A command palette resolving destinations, views and issues, derived from components/nav/config.ts rather than a second hardcoded list — its round-trip test verifies a token resolves back to its own destination and view AT RUNTIME, so a renamed view cannot silently land on the destination default. The sprint-to-bolt rename is pinned by test. A foreign task_key does not leak: from a Limiglow page TOD-1 renders 'not found in Limiglow' with no trace of the other project in the DOM. No new API surface was added, on the grounds that a second issues-reading endpoint is a second place the boundary must be re-derived. Held back: Enter lands on Work then List rather than the issue, because no issue route exists, and the palette carries no verbs.
channels.goal_text: Slack search — modifiers like in:, from:, before: that narrow 2,440 records to the one you meant, and results that open in context rather than a dead list.
